findings.text: next_sequence globs '*/measurement.json' relative to the directory run_cases.py:301 passes, which is the job's own output directory whose receipt sits at its top level, so a fresh job always returns 1 (probe: a job directory holding measurement.json with sequence 1 yields next_sequence 1), and a re-measured arm ties the first run instead of superseding it; the run directory's 1..10 sequences were backfilled by hand in one batch (eight receipts share mtime 06:19:20, mastu-displaced3 and mastu-titan2 are 06:31:41, tcv-iter-long is 08:21:22), so the ordering the record relies on is not produced by this code.

the ordering test constructs the nested run/arm layout the reader expects and never calls next_sequence through run_cases' job-directory layout, so it stays green while the writer emits sequence 1 and guards the read half of the capability only.

baseline_suite cites armed-baseline.log, whose second line is '# tree /tmp/ssr-base-arm', so records.suite_arm_log:135 raises ValueError on the very log the manifest names and the base arm's revision and command cannot be read back through the reader the same commit added.

a preview PNG is committed although report.py:98-103 states previews are not published and the fragment cites neither preview, and panels.py:190-191 writes one beside every panel so the uncited raster enters docs/figures.

the recorded last finite residuals (mastu-stored-default 4.70674, mastu-displaced-default 5.03224, tcv-stored-default 0.905546) sit orders of magnitude from §1's 4.9e-10, 1.2e-4 and 0.030, and mastu-stored-continuation refused with 0 finite entries instead of qualifying below 1e-10, so §1's done_when (1) and (2) remain unmet and belong to §2/§3.
